name: Rockwell Automation, Inc.
fiscal_year_note: Fiscal year ends Sep 30. FY2026 = Oct 1, 2025 to Sep 30, 2026 (Q1 Oct-Dec, Q2 Jan-Mar, Q3 Apr-Jun, Q4 Jul-Sep). Q4/full-year FY2026 results and first FY2027 guidance are scheduled for Thursday Nov 5, 2026 (pre-market is Rockwell's usual timing); annual investor meeting Nov 18, 2026 alongside Automation Fair. The Sensia oil & gas JV (formerly in Lifecycle Services) was dissolved Apr 1, 2026, so reported growth trails organic growth by about 3 points in H2 FY2026.

latest_quarter.label: Q3 FY2026 (Apr-Jun 2026, quarter ended Jun 30, 2026)
latest_quarter.operating_margin_basis: non-GAAP (enterprise operating margin; GAAP pre-tax margin was 20.3%)

guidance: FY2026 guidance (updated Aug 4, 2026): reported sales growth 7.5%-9.5% (about $9.0B at midpoint; divestitures about -1.5 pts, currency about +1.5 pts), organic growth 7.5%-9.5% (prior 5%-9%; initial Nov 2025 range 2%-6%), adjusted EPS $13.00-$13.30 (prior $12.50-$13.10; initial $11.20-$12.20), GAAP diluted EPS $12.72-$13.02, adjusted tax rate about 19.5%. On the Q3 call management added: FY26 enterprise operating margin about 21.5% (+~260 bps), about 100% free cash flow conversion, about $850M of buybacks, Q4 sales up low single digits sequentially with roughly flat enterprise margin (memory-chip inflation), FY26 capex about 3% of sales and FY27 capex higher but around 4%. FY2027 guidance due Nov 5, 2026.

consensus_next_fy.label: FY2027 (Oct 2026 to Sep 2027)
consensus_next_fy.eps_basis: adjusted (non-GAAP); 27-28 analysts; FY2026 consensus is revenue $9.06B and adjusted EPS $13.24

valuation.basis: pe_forward from stockanalysis at the Oct 26, 2026 close (NTM basis; Yahoo shows 28.6). EV about $50.5B = market cap $47.74B + borrowings $3.26B - cash $0.48B. ev_sales_forward = EV / FY2027 consensus revenue $9.58B. ev_ebitda_forward is an ESTIMATE (see notes); trailing EV/EBITDA is 24.1x per stockanalysis.

physical_ai_exposure.description: Industrial automation pure play: Logix controllers, drives, motion (including MagneMotion and iTRAK independent-cart technology), safety and sensing, FactoryTalk and Plex software, and OTTO/Clearpath autonomous mobile robots (AMRs). Intelligent Devices plus Software & Control were 79% of Q3 FY26 sales. Revenue from dedicated robotics (AMRs, independent cart) is not disclosed; on the Q3 FY26 call management said that business should post another year of strong double-digit growth and reach a clear path to profitability in Q4 FY26.
physical_ai_exposure.optionality_notes: Picks-and-shovels supplier for physical AI in factories and warehouses: e-commerce/warehouse automation sales +30% in Q3 FY26, strong semiconductor and data-center demand (power distribution, chiller controls, Logix in central utility plants), OTTO AMR fleet software, AI software launches (FactoryTalk Conductor AI-native orchestration platform on Oct 21, 2026; NVIDIA Nemotron model support on Oct 22, 2026; generative AI across Plex), SecureOT industrial cybersecurity services, and an electrification partnership with Hitachi Energy (Oct 15, 2026).

backlog_or_pipeline: Total backlog was $2,878M at Sep 30, 2025 (vs $3,091M a year earlier): Intelligent Devices $704M, Software & Control $654M, Lifecycle Services $1,520M (FY2025 10-K). The Jun 30, 2026 10-Q shows about $1,375M of unfulfilled performance obligations (about $820M within 12 months); this is a narrower measure than backlog, and Sensia's backlog left with the JV. Q3 FY26 book-to-bill was inside the normal range (Lifecycle Services 0.97); organic ARR +6% (below expectations), software ARR up high single digits. No order dollar figures are disclosed.
cost_and_supply_chain_notes: About 10 principal manufacturing facilities, the most significant in the US, Mexico, Poland, India, Canada and Singapore; principal distribution centers in the US and the Netherlands; about 26,000 employees at Sep 30, 2025 (9k North America, 5k EMEA, 7k Asia Pacific, 5k Latin America). Broad supplier base but several single-source suppliers; rare-earth minerals flagged as a supply risk. Tariffs are managed with pricing, alternative sourcing and redundant manufacturing; the company expected tariff costs to be EPS-neutral in FY2026. FY26 price realization about 250 bps (about 100 bps tariff-related, about 150 bps underlying). Guidance excludes any IEEPA tariff refunds tied to the Supreme Court decision. Memory-chip inflation driven by data-center demand is a growing double-digit-million headwind in H2 FY26, concentrated in Software & Control margins. FY27 capex about 4% of sales includes a greenfield facility in New Berlin, Wisconsin.
debt_notes: At Jun 30, 2026: short-term debt $686M, of which commercial paper $684M at a 3.89% weighted average rate with about 25-day average maturity (floating, rolls monthly); current portion of long-term debt $2M; long-term debt $2,570M (senior notes; coupon and maturity schedule not retrieved). Interest expense $33M in Q3 FY26 (vs $41M) and $101M for 9M FY26 (vs $119M); FY2025 interest expense, net $143M. In Nov 2025 the company replaced its $1.5B revolver with a new five-year $1.5B unsecured facility expiring Nov 2030 (SOFR-based, expandable by $750M). Sensia's $75M credit line and SLB loans were settled or assumed by SLB at the JV dissolution. Net debt about $2.8B, roughly 1.3x trailing EBITDA of $2.09B. Lease liabilities of about $0.35B are excluded from total_debt_bn.
customer_concentration: No single end customer is disclosed as material. About 65% of global sales go through independent distributors; the two largest distributors were about 20% of total sales in each of FY2023-FY2025. Sales outside the US are less than half of the total; the largest non-US markets are Canada, China, Italy, the UK and Mexico.
key_drivers: US manufacturing investment and reshoring: North America is 64% of sales and grew 12% organically in Q3 FY26; management expects it to be the fastest-growing region in FY26 and cites labor shortages and reshoring as automation drivers.

Discrete end markets: Q3 FY26 discrete sales up high teens, with e-commerce/warehouse +30%, strong semiconductor and data-center demand, and automotive up low double digits with early signs of renewed project activity; hybrid up mid-single digits (life sciences +10%); process up high single digits, led by energy.
Software & Control: organic sales +18% in Q3 FY26 with a 34.8% segment margin (31.6% a year earlier).
Margin expansion from productivity and pricing: enterprise operating margin 22.3% in Q3 FY26 vs 19.5%; FY26 target about 21.5% (+~260 bps); price about 250 bps in FY26.
Capital returns: about $850M of FY26 buybacks, about $1.2B of authorization left after Q3, dividend $1.38 per quarter (about 1.3% yield).
Catalyst: FY2027 guidance on Nov 5, 2026 against consensus FY27 revenue of $9.58B (+5.8%) and adjusted EPS of $14.91 (+12.7%).
Macro sensitivity: orders track US manufacturing capex and the ISM Manufacturing PMI (no current PMI reading was retrieved for this file); in the last industrial downturn FY2024 sales fell 8.8%.
AI and software product cycle: FactoryTalk Conductor (Oct 2026), NVIDIA Nemotron support, Plex generative AI, CompactLogix 5390 controller launch (Oct 13, 2026).
key_risks: Valuation: about 40x trailing GAAP EPS and about 29.6x forward P/E; the stock fell 7.4% on Aug 4, 2026 despite a beat and raise, and 5.4% on Feb 5, 2026 when the guidance midpoint sat below consensus.
Input inflation: memory-chip costs were called a growing double-digit-million headwind in H2 FY26, mainly in Software & Control, and management expects inflation to persist into FY27.
Project delays: greenfield projects are being delayed by tariffs and geopolitical uncertainty; Latin America fell 3% organically in Q3 FY26 and mining was down mid-single digits.
Weak recurring/services growth: Lifecycle Services -2% organic in Q3 FY26 with book-to-bill 0.97; organic ARR growth of 6% was below expectations.
Trade policy: plants in Mexico, Poland, India and Singapore; rare-earth supply risk; tariff pricing is meant to be EPS-neutral but customers may push back.
Channel concentration: the two largest distributors are about 20% of sales.
Cyclicality: FY2024 sales fell 8.8%, and backlog fell from $3.09B to $2.88B during FY2025.
Leadership transitions announced Sep 24, 2026 (details not retrieved).

notes: Price, share count and market cap from stockanalysis.com (close Oct 26, 2026); the 10-Q cover shows 111,048,676 shares at Jun 30, 2026. total_debt_bn = short-term debt $0.686B + current long-term debt $0.002B + long-term debt $2.570B at Jun 30, 2026, excluding about $0.35B of lease liabilities (stockanalysis total debt including leases is $3.61B). cash_and_investments_bn is cash and equivalents only. cash_burn_annual_bn is 0 because free cash flow is positive (LTM +$1.50B). Q3 revenue growth is 7.9% reported (8% rounded) and 10% organic. last_fiscal_year.operating_income_bn ($1.422B) is stockanalysis' standardized operating income; Rockwell itself reports FY2025 segment operating earnings of $1.703B (20.4% margin) and GAAP pre-tax income of $0.917B, the latter depressed by about $0.26B of Lifecycle Services purchase accounting D&A and impairment. ltm figures are from stockanalysis and match hand calculations from company releases. R&D of $0.679B for FY2025 is from SEC XBRL data; the FY2025 10-K recast earlier years upward (FY2024 $0.658B vs $0.477B originally reported). ev_ebitda_forward 21.9x is an ESTIMATE: EV about $50.5B divided by an assumed FY2027 EBITDA of about $2.3B (about 22% enterprise margin on consensus revenue plus about $0.2B of non-acquisition D&A, scaled from Q3 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $565M vs enterprise operating profit of $516M). Beta 1.51 is Yahoo 5Y monthly (stockanalysis 5Y: 1.50). Short interest 3.31% of float is stockanalysis' latest (undated); Yahoo shows 3.75% as of Aug 31, 2026. Geographic and segment mix are Q3 FY26 sales; full-year FY2025 mix was North America 63.2%, EMEA 17.8%, Asia Pacific 12.3%, Latin America 6.7% and Intelligent Devices 45.0%, Software & Control 28.6%, Lifecycle Services 26.4% (pre-Sensia exit). 52-week range $347.53-$497.36; 52-week change about +20%.
